Publish from Rhino#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — upload core tested, plug-in builds, needs a real Rhino install.** The Rhino 8 script imports cleanly outside Rhino and its shared Python helper published GLB, OBJ (with units) and IFC, one-shot and resumable, to a real local Verse server; every scene finished and opened; a dead server and a cancel each gave one plain sentence. The RhinoCommon plug-in compiles for Rhino 7 (net48, RhinoCommon 7) and Rhino 8 (net7.0, RhinoCommon 8) with 0 errors (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). Neither has been run inside Rhino yet.

Two ways in, same flow — Rhino's own glTF exporter writes the model (metres, Y-up, materials and textures), it uploads with progress, and the share link is copied and opened:

Rhino 8 Python scriptRhinoCommon plug-in
Rhino8 (CPython 3)7 and 8, Windows and Mac
StartTools ▸ Script ▸ Run → VersePublishRhino.pyVersePublish command
SettingsSettings option of the scriptVersePublishSettings command
CancelEscEsc

You need: Rhino 8 for the glTF exporter. On Rhino 7 the plug-in loads but there is no glTF exporter: export OBJ or FBX yourself and upload it with python3 verse_upload.py <file> --units <unit>.

1. Install#

Download VersePublish-Rhino-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page once the packages are published, or build it:

Code
sh integrations/aec/rhino/make_package.sh   # -> integrations/aec/rhino/dist/VersePublish-Rhino-4.0.0-beta.1.zip
  • Script: unzip and keep script/ together (VersePublishRhino.py needs verse_upload.py and verse_settings.py beside it). Run it with Tools ▸ Script ▸ Run, or put ! _-RunPythonScript "<path>\VersePublishRhino.py" on a toolbar button.
  • Plug-in: drag build/net48/VersePublishRhino.rhp (Rhino 7, or Rhino 8 on Windows) or build/net7.0/VersePublishRhino.rhp (Rhino 8's .NET 7 runtime) onto Rhino, or Tools ▸ Options ▸ Plug-ins ▸ Install.

2. Server and key#

The script's Settings option and the plug-in's VersePublishSettings both ask for server URL (default https://verse.ctruh.com), API key, account token (from Studio) and bake lighting; the script also has open link and run verse-prepare when found.

Nothing is compiled in. Both store them in the per-user file every Verse plug-in shares — %APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\settings.json on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/Ctruh/VersePublish/settings.json on macOS — in its rhino section, so the script and the plug-in always agree. Values saved as shared from another tool (e.g. "every plug-in" in SketchUp or Revit) apply unless Rhino sets its own. VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY, VERSE_TOKEN override the file. A 4.0.0-beta.1 ~/.verse-publish.json is imported once.

3. Publish#

  1. Script: choose Publish or PublishSelection. Plug-in: run VersePublish (option SelectionOnly).
  2. The status bar / command prompt shows exporting glTF → uploading % → building (stage). Esc cancels and tells you whether anything was published.
  3. Published! — the link is on the clipboard and opens in the browser.

Success looks like: Published! with the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); the model opens at its real size in metres.

If -_Export shows the glTF options dialog the first time, accept the defaults once; Rhino remembers them for scripted exports.

What gets exported#

Everything visible (or the selection), as Rhino 8's glTF exporter writes it: model units converted to metres, Y-up, render materials as PBR with textures. When the bundled verse-prepare is present the script runs it first (verse-prepare). Files over 100 MB use the resumable upload.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in the plug-in's settings (first run, or VersePublishSettings) (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in the plug-in's settings (first run, or VersePublishSettings).
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
"Rhino did not write the glTF file. The glTF exporter needs Rhino 8; …"Rhino 7's script path has no glTF exporter.Use the C# plug-in (.rhp) on Rhino 7, or Rhino 8.
"Nothing is selected. Select the objects to publish, or turn off 'selection only'."PublishSelection with nothing selected.Select objects, or run Publish.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.
